title: "Font Can't Be Embedded Due to Licensing": How to Fix It (KDP & IngramSpark) | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix "font cannot be embedded because of licensing restrictions"
description: Some fonts don't allow embedding, so your PDF can't carry them and the printer rejects it. How to spot them and swap them out quickly.
platforms: Amazon KDP · IngramSpark · Barnes & Noble Press · Lulu
lead: Printers need every font built into your PDF. Some fonts' licenses say no, and that blocks the whole file.
error: Font cannot be embedded because of licensing restrictions
errorNote: Paraphrased. Word, Acrobat and printers each word this a little differently.
why:
Every font comes with a license. Some licenses don't allow the font to be put inside a PDF ("embedded"). When you export, the font is left out, and the printer's system either rejects the file or swaps in a different font, which can change your line breaks and page count.

It's common with fonts downloaded from free font sites and some older system fonts.
manual: Open your file and list the fonts you used (Word: Home → Replace → Format → Font, or check the PDF in Acrobat: File → Properties → Fonts).
Find the fonts that aren't embedded or that warn about licensing.
Replace them with fonts whose license allows embedding, such as open-license (OFL) fonts.
Re-export as PDF/X-1a:2001 and confirm every font now says "Embedded".
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.

cta.text: SparkPrep checks every font in your file, flags the ones that can't be embedded, and the Interior Studio's fonts are all open-license and safe to print.

faq.q: Which fonts are safe to embed for printing?
faq.a: Open-license (OFL) fonts, like most on Google Fonts, allow embedding. Check the license of any font from a free font site.

faq.q: Will the printer replace a missing font?
faq.a: Some systems swap in a different font, which can change your layout. Most printers reject the file instead.
